    behavioral: wire V-state transport across vsim boundaries
    
    Three coordinated changes that together let RVV C-level fixtures
    round-trip v0..v31 through the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 hybrid handoff:
    
    1. apply_resume_from_qemu (simulator.hpp): when the inbound state
       has HYBRID_FLAG_V set, copy state.vreg[] into the fixed scratch
       region of guest RAM via stage_v_to_scratch. The fixture's
       vsim-phase prologue (vle8.v vN, (scratch)) reads it back to
       repopulate the regfile.
    
    2. check_hybrid_handoff (simulator.hpp): when the drain produces a
       state with HYBRID_FLAG_V set, copy scratch RAM bytes back into
       state.vreg[] via read_v_from_scratch before writing the file out.
       This captures any V-reg modifications the fixture made (the
       fixture's epilogue writes vse8.v vN, (scratch) to settle the
       bytes).
    
    3. ResumeDriver (resume_driver.hpp): also restore mtvec via the DM
       Abstract Command path. Otherwise vsim resumes with mtvec=0 and
       any in-vsim trap re-traps at the zero-mapped vector, hanging the
       sim. mstatus / vtype / vl are intentionally NOT restored: vsim's
       DM may not honor abstract-write of mstatus (fixture uses csrs to
       set VS itself), and direct CSR write of vtype sets vill (per V
       spec, vtype must only change via vsetvli).
    
    4. spawn_qemu (qemu_handback.hpp): pass `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`
       to QEMU 2. The default `rv64` CPU has no V extension; mstatus.VS
       is then read-only zero, and the fixture's csrs / vsetvli in
       Phase 3 traps with illegal-instruction. Also ensures Andes
       vendor CSRs (mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl) match QEMU 1.
    
    5. rt_c_v_regs.c: rewritten to do all V work inside the vsim phase
       (Phase A in QEMU 1 only seeds memory). The QEMU plugin's
       gdbstub-pc readback misreports the drain PC when V instructions
       are in flight in QEMU 1 - keeping V purely on the vsim side
       sidesteps that. Phase 3 (in QEMU 2) sets mstatus.VS via csrs
       before vsetvli, since the gdbstub mstatus restore may not carry
       VS through cleanly.

      bash run_e2e.sh

1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <span>
18	#include <stdexcept>
19	#include <string>
20	
21	namespace hybrid {
22	
23	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
24	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
25	
26	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
27	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
28	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
29	
30	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
31	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
32	
33	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
34	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
35	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
36	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
37	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
38	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
39	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
41	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
42	
43	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
44	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
45	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
46	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
47	{
48	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
49	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
50	         | (0b001u << 12)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
52	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
53	}
54	
55	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
56	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
57	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
58	//
59	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
60	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
61	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
62	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
63	// surfacing the fault.
64	template<typename Bus>
65	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
66	{
67	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
68	        throw std::runtime_error(
69	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
70	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
71	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
72	
73	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
74	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
75	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
76	
77	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
78	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
79	
80	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
81	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
82	
83	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
84	    if (cmderr != 0u)
85	        throw std::runtime_error(
86	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
87	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
88	}
89	
90	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
91	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
92	// function so every DM client shares one copy.
93	template<typename Bus>
94	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
95	{
96	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
97	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
98	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
99	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
100	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
101	                     "write_register_abstract");
102	}
103	
104	}  // namespace hybrid

The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for v0..v31, so the
V data regfile moves through a scratch page at the TOP of the shared mmap
(v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES, L26): the

pb_v_data_sweep runs vsetvl-led vle8.v/vse8.v sweeps on the halted hart
through the Program Buffer, so benchmark binaries carry no transport code.
The sweep is LMUL=8-grouped from day one: the scratch is packed at vlenb
stride, one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole 8-register group, and the in-buffer
addi advances the base pointer x7, so all 32 registers transfer in one
vsetvl plus one grouped PB execution (each execution is a ~1000-cycle DM
round-trip, so the execution count is the cost). ResumeDriver restores in
a fixed order -- mstatus.VS enable, data reload sweep, Tier-B vtype+vl via
